lessons.title: Science measures the world
lessons.summary: Scientists use standard constants and units so experiments can be compared anywhere in the world.

question.q: What is the speed of light in a vacuum?
question.hint: It is about 300 million meters per second.
question.explain: The speed of light in a vacuum is about 3 x 10^8 meters per second.

lessons.title: Chemistry uses symbols as shorthand
lessons.summary: Chemical formulas tell you which atoms are present and how many of each are bonded together.

question.q: What is the chemical formula for water?
question.hint: Two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
question.explain: Water is H2O: two hydrogen atoms bonded to one oxygen atom.

lessons.title: Units help engineers communicate
lessons.summary: Each physical quantity has a standard unit so people do not confuse current, force, energy, or power.

question.hint: It is named after Andre-Marie Ampere.
question.explain: The ampere is the SI unit for electrical current.

lessons.title: Acceleration changes velocity
lessons.summary: If an object starts from rest and accelerates steadily, its velocity grows linearly with time.

question.q: An object starts from rest and accelerates at 5 m/s^2. What is its velocity after 3 seconds?
question.hint: Start with u = 0 and use v = u + at.

lessons.title: Force and acceleration are linked
lessons.summary: Newton's second law says acceleration increases with force and decreases with mass.

question.q: A 10 kg object has a net force of 30 N. What is its acceleration?
question.hint: Rearrange the formula to a = F / m.

lessons.title: Motion stores energy
lessons.summary: Moving objects carry kinetic energy, and that energy increases with the square of speed.

question.q: What is the kinetic energy of a 2 kg object moving at 4 m/s?

lessons.title: Elements are defined by protons
lessons.summary: An element's atomic number tells you how many protons are in its nucleus.

question.q: What is the atomic number of carbon?
question.explain: Carbon's atomic number is 6 because it has 6 protons.

lessons.title: Atoms bond in different ways
lessons.summary: Covalent bonds share electrons, while ionic bonds transfer them.

question.q: Which type of bond involves sharing electrons?
question.hint: Think of atoms holding electrons together.
question.explain: Covalent bonds form when atoms share electron pairs.

lessons.title: Chemists count in moles
lessons.summary: A mole is a counting unit for atoms and molecules, just like a dozen is a counting unit for eggs.

question.q: How many particles are in one mole?

lessons.title: Derivatives measure change
lessons.summary: The derivative tells you how quickly one quantity changes as another changes.

question.q: What is the derivative of x^3?
question.hint: Bring the exponent down and subtract one from the power.

lessons.title: Linear equations encode rate
lessons.summary: In y = mx + b, the slope m tells you how much y changes when x increases by one.

question.q: What is the slope of y = 3x + 5?
question.hint: The slope is the coefficient of x.
question.explain: In y = 3x + 5, the slope m is 3.

lessons.title: Geometry turns shape into measurement
lessons.summary: Area formulas let you compare how much space different shapes cover.

question.q: What is the area of a circle with radius 2?
question.hint: Square the radius before multiplying by pi.

lessons.title: Circuits connect voltage, current, and resistance
lessons.summary: Ohm's law is one of the first tools engineers use to predict electrical behavior.

question.q: If current is 2 A and resistance is 5 ohms, what is the voltage?
question.explain: V = I x R = 2 x 5 = 10 V.

lessons.title: Distributed loads add up
lessons.summary: Engineers often convert load per unit length into total load before analyzing structures.
lessons.formula: total load = load per length x length

question.q: What is the total load of 10 N/m over 4 m?
question.hint: Multiply the distributed load by the full length.

lessons.title: Efficiency compares useful output to input
lessons.summary: No real machine is perfectly efficient, so engineers compare useful energy out to total energy in.

question.q: A machine gives 80 J of useful output from 100 J of input. What is its efficiency?
question.hint: Divide useful output by total input, then convert to percent.
